newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR TAKES UP COACHING ASSIGNMENT FOR ZIMBABWE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR TAKES UP COACHING ASSIGNMENT FOR ZIMBABWE.

text.p: Bruce Grobbelaar makes the transition from eccentric goalkeeper to coach when Zimbabwe meet Tanzania in an international on Sunday.
The 38-year-old goalkeeper, who faces trial in Britain on charges of match-fixing, was last month appointed acting co-coach with Meshack Marimo, a former Zimbabwe international.
Grobbelaar, who now plays for Plymouth Argyle in the English second division, arrived from London on Tuesday to take charge of the team.
Sunday's match, the opening game in a new regional five-nation competition, is Grobbelaar's first managerial job. He said on Friday he was enjoying the experience.
One of his first decisions will be to put himself back in goal after missing Zimbabwe's last four internationals.
"I am going to play," he said.
Grobbelaar travelled with Zimbabwe to Madagascar in June for their World Cup preliminary round tie but was not chosen to play by previous coach Marc Duvillard.
He and Marimo have chosen a youthful squad for Sunday's international, which comes two weeks ahead of the country's opening 1998 African Nations Cup qualifying group match in the Sudan.

Zimbabwe are also involved in key World Cup qualifying matches in November. Grobbelaar believes his team have a strong chance of qualifying from the group in which their opponents are Angola, Cameroon and Togo.

Grobbelaar, fellow goalkeeper Hans Segers, retired striker John Fashanu and Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim pleaded not guilty in May to charges of giving or accepting bribes to fix English premier league matches. The trial is scheduled for January.
